terms.brief: The Python/PyTorch environment the software runs on
terms.detail: The synthesis engine runs on Python with PyTorch. It is not part of the installer; on first launch the matching build is downloaded for your graphics card.

terms.brief: The character’s .ckpt, which controls phrasing and rhythm
terms.detail: Controls pause cadence, stress placement, and intonation contours, determining the prosody of synthesized speech. It turns text into semantic tokens and determines phrasing, stress, and tone. It is the .ckpt file in a voice pack.

terms.brief: The character’s .pth, which controls the timbre
terms.detail: Renders prosodic features into the target speaker's vocal timbre and acoustic texture, determining voice similarity. It turns semantic tokens into a waveform and determines the timbre. It is the .pth file in a voice pack. The two weights must be used as a matched pair; a mismatched pair produces noise.

terms.brief: The clip that sets the voice and emotion of a synthesis
terms.detail: A real recording of the voice that the model hears during synthesis. Timbre, pace, and emotion follow it, so the same text sounds different with another reference. Clean clips of 3–10 seconds work best.

terms.brief: The exact words spoken in the reference clip
terms.detail: Enter the exact transcript and punctuation spoken in the reference audio; mismatches between transcript and audio may cause skipped words or timbre distortion. It must match the audio exactly; otherwise the model misjudges the pronunciation and the voice becomes unstable. Voice packs already include it in their .list files, so it rarely needs to be entered by hand.

terms.brief: The dataset index: path, speaker, language, text
terms.detail: The GPT-SoVITS dataset format, one entry per line: audio path | speaker | language | text. Review it on the Annotate page before training. Entries whose text does not match the audio cause pronunciation errors.

terms.brief: Which language’s rules turn text into sounds
terms.detail: Determines how the text is read and does not depend on the voice. For mixed Chinese and English text, choose a mixed mode so the engine decides segment by segment. The most common sign of a wrong language is English words read as pinyin.

terms.brief: How long text is broken into pieces before synthesis
terms.detail: The model works best with about one sentence at a time, so long text is split first. Splitting by punctuation sounds most natural; splitting by length is more even and suits text without punctuation. Splitting too finely breaks the flow between segments.

terms.brief: Overall faster or slower; 1.0 is unchanged
terms.detail: Changes the duration after synthesis without generating again, so the reading itself does not change. Large changes sound noticeably sped up or slowed down; values between 0.8 and 1.2 are recommended.

terms.brief: How many of the likeliest tokens each step may choose from
terms.detail: Smaller values are more conservative: the reading is stable but flatter. Larger values add variation in tone and also more mistakes. The default is 15, which rarely needs changing.

terms.brief: How much the delivery is allowed to vary
terms.detail: Lower values are more predictable, and the same text is read almost identically each time. Higher values add more emotional range and more unclear articulation. The default is 1.0.

s.mainGpuTip:
Selects which NVIDIA GPU performs the computation when more than one is installed.
The engine defaults to the lowest-numbered device. On a computer with both a 5060 and a 5090, that default is often not the faster card.
Changes take effect from the next synthesis or training run.
If a task fails to start after changing this, or reports insufficient VRAM, set it back to Automatic first: when the selected index does not match a device the driver actually reports, the engine finds no GPU and falls back to a slower mode.
s.computeBackendTip:
The device the engine is actually computing on.
The backend is chosen automatically: CUDA when available, CPU otherwise. On CPU, synthesis is much slower; on some machines a virtual display adapter gets picked and the engine then reports insufficient VRAM.
If what you see here is not what you expect, check the main graphics card setting and your display driver.

synth.auxEmpty: Hover a reference and click the plus button to add it as an auxiliary reference for timbre blending.
synth.batchPlaceholder: One item per line. Items are synthesized in order.
synth.pBatchTip: Number of segments inferred in parallel. Larger values speed up long text but use more VRAM.
synth.pFragmentTip: Silence inserted between adjacent synthesized segments.
synth.pRepTip: Penalizes repetition. Too low causes loops; too high hurts fluency.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Complete instructions from installation to training. Hints in the app link directly to the matching section.
help.frQ1: What should I do on first launch?
help.frA1: On first launch, the app detects the GPU and downloads the matching runtime environment (about 6 GB for NVIDIA, less for CPU), then opens the home page. This happens only once; keep the network connected.
help.frQ2: Where do base models come from?
help.frA2: Synthesis and training need engine resources such as HuBERT, the text feature model, and the GPT-SoVITS base models. The app asks whether to download them on first launch, and they can be downloaded at any time under Plaza → Download models.
help.frQ3: How do I install a character pack?
help.frA3: On the Models page, click Import pack and choose the .zip file. The voice then appears in the voice lists on the home page and the Synthesize page.
help.packQ1: What is inside a character pack?
help.packA1: A SoVITS timbre model, a GPT prosody model, a reference set (.list annotations), cover art and recommended parameters, packaged as one zip.
help.packQ2: What does the reference audio do?
help.packA2: GPT-SoVITS is few-shot cloning: the model imitates the delivery of the selected reference clip. Switching references changes emotion and pacing.
help.packQ3: Can I package my own trained model?
help.packA3: Yes. After training, the voice appears on the Models page. Choose Export pack from its menu to get a zip file that can be shared.
help.synthQ1: Why doesn't the output match the expected character?
help.synthA1: Make sure the reference comes from the target character's annotations and that text language matches (or use auto). For cross-lingual text prefer a same-language reference.
help.synthQ2: Output loops or breaks up. What should I adjust?
help.synthA2: Raise repetition_penalty or lower temperature for loops; lower top_k for broken or missing syllables. Compare with the same text after each tweak.
help.synthA3: With streaming on, the first audio chunk returns before the whole utterance finishes, cutting perceived latency on long texts. Turn it off for export-grade takes.
help.synthA4: The Synthesize page splits the text automatically with the chosen splitting method and synthesizes it segment by segment. No manual splitting is needed.
help.trainQ1: What do I need to train a character?
help.trainA1: Prepare at least 5 minutes of speech with no background music and a consistent volume. If the material comes from songs or has reverb, remove the accompaniment first with vocal separation on the Train page.
help.trainA2: The Annotate page opens an existing .list file for line-by-line review. If the dataset has no .list, training first slices the audio and then creates the annotation with a transcription model (one must be installed).
help.trainQ3: How do I use a finished model?
help.trainA3: After training, the voice is saved to the voice folder and appears on the Models page. It can be used on the Synthesize page right away.
help.listA1: Each line has four columns separated by vertical bars: audio path|speaker|language|text, for example audios/demo.wav|Name|ZH|Hello. The audio path is relative to the folder of the .list file.
help.listA2: ZH, JA, EN, KO, YUE. Annotations may be split per language, e.g. name_JP.list alongside name_ZH.list.
help.listQ3: How much does annotation quality matter?
help.listA3: The text annotation is the basis of training quality. Wrong annotations harm both timbre and prosody. Before training, listen to and review each line on the Annotate page, paying particular attention to characters with several readings and to numbers.
help.faqQ1: Can I use it without an NVIDIA GPU?
help.faqA1: Yes. Without an NVIDIA GPU, the app synthesizes with the CPU runtime. It is slower but fully functional; 8 GB of memory or more is recommended. Training requires an NVIDIA GPU.
help.faqQ2: Can models of different versions be mixed?
help.faqA2: No. The versions (v2, v2Pro, v2ProPlus, v4, V5, and others) have different base models and network structures. The SoVITS and GPT weights of one voice must come from the same version.
help.faqA3: The Synthesize page manages loaded models automatically. If GPU memory is still insufficient, shorten the text, close other programs that use GPU memory, or turn off streaming.
help.faqQ4: How do I share a character?
help.faqA4: Open the voice’s menu on the Models page and choose Export pack. Send the resulting zip file to others; they can use it after importing it on their Models page.

runtime.title: Runtime environment
runtime.body: Synthesis and training require the runtime. The app downloads and installs it on first launch.

role.title: Voice
role.body: Synthesis requires at least one voice. Download one from the Plaza, import a voice pack, or train one from your own recordings.

synth.title: First synthesis
synth.body: On the Synthesize page, choose a voice and a reference clip, enter the text, and start synthesis.

own.title: Your own voice
own.body: Prepare the recordings and their text on the Annotate page, then start training on the Train page. The new voice appears on the Models page when training finishes.

notice.title: Before you start
notice.where: Report problems in the QQ group or on GitHub Issues. Requests for help in comment sections are not handled.

notice.detail: Describe the steps you took, the messages you saw, and the result you expected.
